title: Desk Guidance — Coverage Verification and the Financial Class of a Patient Financial Account
content:
The tier recorded on a Patient Financial Account is the financial class of the patient's primary coverage as verified with the payer. The tier that governs a charge is the tier whose coverage was in force on that charge's date of service.

## Activation

An account is activated once the payer's eligibility response confirms the coverage — or, for the Self-Pay Account, once the uninsured attestation is signed. The primary care copay, the specialist copay and the remaining deductible returned by the payer are recorded with the verification date.

## Reported changes of coverage

- When a patient reports new or changed insurance, the payer name and the member number are recorded exactly as printed on the card; the tier becomes the financial class whose entry criteria the new coverage meets; and the coverage effective date recorded is the effective date on the card.
- A patient who reports losing all coverage moves to the Self-Pay Account from the date coverage ended.
- A patient-described plan that matches no class's entry criteria — for example an out-of-state Medicaid plan or a plan not contracted with the group — is not recorded as insured. The account stays on its current tier, and the services are handled as self-pay unless the patient presents a qualifying coverage.

## When a coverage update may be recorded

A coverage update is recorded only while the account is open: its status is registered, active, billing hold, precollection or collections when the update is recorded. The status is taken from the account record for that same account at the time of the update. A closed account receives no coverage update.

| Account status at the time of the update | Coverage update recorded? |
|---|---|
| registered, active, billing hold, precollection, collections | yes |
| closed | no |

## Re-verification

Coverage must be re-verified — by a coverage update that sets the coverage verified date to the handling date — whenever more than the tier's re-verification period, in calendar days, has passed since the coverage verified date and a new charge is about to be billed to the payer. The two parts of this condition are read together: the time passed since the coverage verified date, and a new charge about to be billed to the payer.

**Hypothetical boundary.** On a tier whose re-verification period is 90 days, for an account verified on day 0 the time part of the condition is met from day 91 onward (more than 90 days have passed) and is not yet met on day 90 (exactly 90 days have passed).
